# Overview of Part 02: Data Wrangling

Up to 80% of any data science project is spent importing, cleaning, transforming, and joining data. Part 02 covers the complete modern R data-wrangling toolkit:

1. **`01_data_import_export_tidyr.R`** — Fast file I/O (`readr`, `.rds`) and reshaping untidy data (`tidyr::pivot_longer`, `pivot_wider`).
2. **`02_dplyr_data_manipulation.R`** — The grammar of data manipulation (`filter`, `select`, `mutate`, `across`, `summarise`, window functions, and relational joins).
3. **`03_strings_factors_dates.R`** — Text processing & regular expressions (`stringr`), factor engineering (`forcats`), and date-time arithmetic (`lubridate`).

---

# Tidy Data & Reshaping

A dataset is **tidy** when:

1. Each variable is in its own column.
2. Each observation is in its own row.
3. Each value is in its own cell.

```{r tidy-reshape}
wide_metrics <- data.frame(
  model    = c("RandomForest", "XGBoost", "LightGBM"),
  acc_2025 = c(0.88, 0.91, 0.90),
  acc_2026 = c(0.90, 0.94, 0.93)
)

# Base R / tidyr reshaping demonstration
if (requireNamespace("tidyr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(tidyr)
  tidy_metrics <- wide_metrics |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("acc_"),
      names_to = "year",
      names_prefix = "acc_",
      values_to = "accuracy"
    )
} else {
  tidy_metrics <- data.frame(
    model    = rep(wide_metrics$model, each = 2),
    year     = rep(c("2025", "2026"), times = 3),
    accuracy = c(t(as.matrix(wide_metrics[, 2:3])))
  )
}
knitr::kable(tidy_metrics, caption = "Tidy Model Accuracy Table")
```

# Mastering `dplyr` Pipelines & Joins

## The 6 Core Verbs of `dplyr`

| Verb | Purpose | SQL Equivalent |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `filter()` | Subset rows by logical condition | `WHERE` / `HAVING` |
| `select()` | Pick or drop columns by name or predicate | `SELECT` |
| `arrange()` | Reorder rows ascending or `desc()` | `ORDER BY` |
| `mutate()` | Create or transform columns | Computed columns |
| `group_by()` | Partition rows into groups | `GROUP BY` |
| `summarise()` | Collapse groups into single-row summaries | Aggregate functions (`SUM`, `AVG`) |

```{r dplyr-demo}
# Using built-in `mtcars` dataset
mtcars_df <- mtcars
mtcars_df$model <- rownames(mtcars)

if (requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(dplyr)
  cyl_summary <- mtcars_df |>
    mutate(kpl = mpg * 0.425144, hp_per_ton = hp / wt) |>
    group_by(cyl) |>
    summarise(
      n_cars       = n(),
      avg_mpg      = round(mean(mpg), 1),
      avg_hp_ton   = round(mean(hp_per_ton), 1),
      top_car      = model[which.max(mpg)],
      .groups      = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(avg_mpg))
} else {
  cyl_summary <- aggregate(cbind(mpg, hp) ~ cyl, data = mtcars_df, FUN = mean)
}

knitr::kable(cyl_summary, caption = "Grouped Vehicle Performance Summary by Cylinder Count")
```

# Strings, Regular Expressions, Factors & Dates

## Extracting Structured Fields from Unstructured Text

```{r regex-extraction}
product_codes <- c("SKU-9041-PRO ($149.99)", "SKU-1022-STD ($49.50)", "SKU-8830-ENT ($499.00)")

sku_id <- sub(".*(SKU-[0-9]+-[A-Z]+).*", "\\1", product_codes)
price  <- as.numeric(sub(".*\\$([0-9.]+)\\).*", "\\1", product_codes))

knitr::kable(data.frame(raw = product_codes, sku_id = sku_id, price_usd = price))
```

## Date-Time Arithmetic

```{r dates-demo}
launch_date <- as.Date("2026-01-15")
milestones  <- seq(from = launch_date, by = "3 months", length.out = 4)

milestone_df <- data.frame(
  milestone = paste("Phase", 1:4),
  date      = milestones,
  day_name  = format(milestones, "%A"),
  days_from_launch = as.numeric(milestones - launch_date)
)
knitr::kable(milestone_df, caption = "Project Roadmap Milestones")
```
